summary: Section Review B, limited. No Blocker and no Major. The out folder policy of pin P6 holds for the cases that the brief names: a '..' segment, a leading dash, a folder of another version, a symlink in the root path, and a symlink in the target folder all give a refusal. The argv check accepts whole numbers only and refuses 1e0, 0x2, 2.0, a huge number, a newline, a Unicode digit, and a repeated flag. All spawns use an argv array, and no user value reaches a shell. A single-file write uses the flag wx and refuses an existing symlink. Three Minor findings remain, each with a proof or a code reading. First, a reader file name in pictures.json has no pattern check, so a crafted slug can write one new PNG outside the out folder (F1). Second, a symlink at a subfolder of an existing out folder can redirect the writes outside the folder (F2, proven by probe). Third, a failed build removes nothing, so a partial print file can stay (F3). Each Minor needs a write-access precondition on committed data or on the out folder, so none is a Major. Six Nit findings follow. The paid-call guard of sub-step 2.8a is not reviewable at this head.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Minor] review-b: Item 4 and item 1, reader file names are not validated. questReaders takes cover.fileName and cover.lineArtFileName from pictures.json with no pattern check, and takes the slug with the regex (.+). A slug such as 'A/../../../tmp/x' passes the regex, and readerStem builds 'l2-w01-A/../../../tmp/x', so path.join(outDir, 'readers-a3', stem + '-a3-cover.png') resolves to '/tmp/x-a3-cover.png', outside the out folder (probe line SLUG joined). The picture read path joins the same unchecked name to the pictures folder. The write uses wx, so the file is new and the bytes are a rendered cover, not chosen bytes. The precondition is a committed edit of content/storytime/l2/print/pictures.json plus a valid 4000 x 3000 PNG at the normalized read path. The shipped 14 rows pass the D-A8 patterns (Review C part 5). Location: dashboard/lib/storytime/print/cover-quest.ts:615-627 and dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:403-404, 413-415, 576, 988. Fix: in questReaders, test fileName and lineArtFileName with an exact pattern such as /^l2-w\d{2}-cover-[a-z0-9-]+-v1(-line)?\.png$/ and throw on a mismatch. In the build, assert that each resolved write path starts with outDir plus the path separator before the write. Rated Minor because the threat needs a tampered data commit; raise to Major only if the owner counts a data-only pull request as in scope.

F2 [Minor] review-b: Item 1, a symlink at a subfolder of the out folder is not refused. checkQuestOutDir checks only the out folder. planQuestBuild follows a symlink at student, teacher, readers-a3, or readers-leaf with existsSync and statSync, and it refuses only a non-empty target. mkdirSync with recursive accepts the link. The probe made out/student a symlink to an empty folder: checkQuestOutDir returned [], planQuestBuild returned no error for the entry, and a wx write to out/student/front.png created the file in the other folder (probe line SUBLINK write landed outside => true). The precondition is that a user or a process with write access to the out folder already placed the link. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:599-612 and :963. Fix: use lstatSync on the four subfolders and refuse a symlink, or create each subfolder with mkdirSync without recursive and compare its realpath with path.join(realish(outDir), folder).

F3 [Minor] review-b: Item 1, a failed build leaves partial files and may leave a partial print file. main has no cleanup in the catch or in the early return paths. The folders, build-report.json, the PNG pages, and the Chrome PDFs stay after a failure. In the --print step, execFileSync throws when make-pdfx fails at group N: the print files of the groups before N stay, and a partial file of group N can stay if Ghostscript does not delete its output. The print file has the final deliverable name. I did not run Ghostscript, so the partial file case is a code reading. A rerun is refused by the plan with the message 'the build never overwrites a file', so the operator must clear the folder by hand. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:1002-1063 and :1068-1070. Fix: write all files into a temp folder next to the out folder and rename the set to the out folder after the last check, or record each created path and remove it in the catch.

F4 [Nit] review-b: Item 1, create-only holds for the files that writeNew creates, but not for three other writers. page.pdf in renderPagePdf (line 864) and the Ghostscript output of make-pdfx (-sOutputFile) do not use wx, and mkdirSync recursive follows a link. The plan-time check that every subfolder is empty is the only guard, so a race between the plan and the write is possible. The probe confirmed that wx refuses an existing symlink file with EEXIST and that the victim file stays unchanged. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:864 and :1061. Fix: write the Chrome PDF to the temp folder and copy it with the flag wx; accept the make-pdfx gap as a record.

F5 [Nit] review-b: Item 2, two path arguments are loose. The probe shows that --print-ready-root '' is accepted and gives the relative root 'storytime/covers-quest-v1' (the current folder), and a root with a newline is accepted. --out '' passes the parser and main resolves it to the current folder, which checkQuestOutDir then refuses. A leading-zero version such as 01 is accepted as 1. The root is user-chosen by design, so no refusal bypass exists. No value reaches a shell. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:301-306 and :316-317. Fix: refuse an empty value and a value with a control character, and require an absolute --print-ready-root.

F6 [Nit] review-b: Item 1, two symlink cases pass the check by design of the resolve rule. A --out symlink that resolves to the right folder is accepted (probe: OUT symlink to the right folder => []). A target folder that is a dangling symlink passes checkQuestOutDir (existsSync is false for a dangling link), and the later mkdirSync throws ENOENT, so no file is written (probe: DANGLING mkdir => throws ENOENT). The brief text 'a symlink is refused' is stricter than the code. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:338-349 and :360-381. Fix: use lstatSync in realish and refuse a symlink at the out folder or record the resolve rule as the contract.

F7 [Nit] review-b: Item 4, a symlink art file is read without a containment check. The art path is path.join(picturesDir, name), and sharp and the Chrome file URL both follow a symlink. --pictures-dir takes any folder. The art name of quest.json has the pattern check, so a link needs a committed symlink with the exact name, and the target must be a PNG of the exact size without alpha. The impact is a read of one picture that the cover then embeds. Location: dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-storytime-quest-covers.ts:544-545, :576-577, :972-975, :988. Fix: compare fs.realpathSync(file) with the realpath of picturesDir and refuse a file outside it.

F8 [Nit] review-b: Item 3, the header says the script makes no network call, but --print starts make-pdfx.ts, which downloads an ICC profile from Adobe on first use with no hash check (make-pdfx.ts:43-58). The code is older than the Phase 2 diff and the profile is cached after the first run. All spawns of the build use an argv array: execFileSync('pdfinfo', ['-box', file]), execFileSync(process.execPath, questPdfxArgs(...)), and spawnSync('gs', [...]) in make-pdfx. Playwright starts Chrome. No shell: true, no exec, and no command string exist. Location: dashboard/scripts/print/make-pdfx.ts:43-58. Fix: pin a sha256 of the profile file or state the first-use download in the script header.

F9 [Nit] review-b: Item 5, paid-call guard of sub-step 2.8a. Not reviewable at this head; covered by the 2.8a guard proof. options/gen_art_final.py does not exist at this head, and Task 2.8 makes it with its own guard table (test-strategy section 4.9, 7 cases and 4 mutants). Review B did not review gen_art.py. Location: measure/runs/storytime_cover_options_20261106/. Fix: none at this head.
evidence: Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD gave 6cceee913701f1859e9f1d37eadfbce8f7671ee5, equal to audited_head_sha and role_base_sha. The sha256 of make-storytime-quest-covers.ts is a3c822fd369316bf7c98ce091948fa3984f25b4a95018b2885935ea8e35ae403, equal to the brief. The script is 1086 lines and the review read all of it.

Item 1, out folder policy: checkQuestOutDir (script lines 360-381) refuses an empty value, a leading dash, any '..' segment, and a resolved path that differs from realish(root/storytime/covers-quest-v<n>), and it refuses a base that differs from realish(root) plus storytime plus the folder name. Probe: a version mismatch folder gives a refusal. The Green test file quest-cover-build.test.ts pins a '..' path, a '..' path to print-v3, an inside link to print-v3, and a target folder that is a symlink out of the root (test lines 559-619). The plan refuses any entry in the four subfolders, with a separate message for a name that the build does not write (script lines 599-612). Gaps: F2, F3, F4, F6.

Item 1, create-only: writeNew uses the flag wx (line 819-821) for the PNG pages, the build reports, and the temp HTML files. Probe: wx on an existing symlink gave EEXIST and the victim file kept its content 'keep'.

Item 2, argv probe through parseQuestArgs (no file read, no spawn): version 1e0, 0x2, 2.0, 99999999999999999999, 4294967296, a trailing newline, and the Arabic-Indic digit were refused; 4294967295 and 01 were accepted; a repeated --level was refused; --out -x was refused ('needs a value') and --pictures-dir followed by --print was refused; an unknown flag such as --exec was refused. The check is /^\d+$/ with Number.isSafeInteger and a range, and the JavaScript $ does not match before a trailing newline. Level and unit accept 1 to 4 only.

Item 3, spawn: the only child process imports of the script are execFileSync. The three calls are pdfinfo with an argv array (line 868), process.execPath with the array of questPdfxArgs (line 1061), and Chrome through Playwright chromium.launch with channel only (line 1034). make-pdfx.ts uses spawnSync with an argv array for gs, unzip, and the pre-conversion (lines 36, 53, 142, 157). No call passes shell: true. The input and output paths of questPdfxArgs are absolute and begin with the out folder, so a value cannot start with a dash.

Item 4, art reads: the book art names come from quest.json and pass checkArtName (Review C part 4). The reader names from pictures.json have no pattern check (F1). The art read has no realpath containment (F7). sharp reads the file with metadata, and Chrome loads it through storytimeCoverFileUrl. The page text goes through esc (cover-quest.ts:376-382), which escapes the five HTML characters.

Probe scope: one tsx script imported the build module and called parseQuestArgs, checkQuestOutDir, and planQuestBuild on temp folders with an empty pictures folder. It launched no Chrome, made no network call, and made no paid call. The script and the temp folders were deleted after the run.

A2 and A6 do not apply: the build reads and writes cover files only, and it does not flip a draft to published status. The brief names no security state that measure/tracks.md calls resolved for this phase, so the A6 check has no claim to test.
commands: grep of make-pdfx.ts for spawn and write calls, of cover-quest.ts for esc and file name use, of quest-cover-build.test.ts for symlink cases
